headline: Elon Musk and Nvidia's Jensen Huang are reported to expect China to close its gap in advanced chip-printing machines by 2030.
score_reason: Pool score 6 lowered by 1: only the headline and a one-sentence preview could be read, so what was said, and when, is unverified.
importance_line: If China did catch up in chip-printing machines, it could weaken Western limits on Chinese chipmaking and affect equipment makers such as ASML, but this is a reported view of two executives, not a result.
summary: Digitimes reports that Elon Musk and Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang see China closing its gap in lithography, the machines that print circuit patterns onto chips, by 2030, while ASML looks at raising output of its most advanced (EUV) machines beyond 110 units by 2028.
notes: Headline and public preview only (Digitimes paywall). Reader level: written at level five as the brief says; Full_Report rules 5.1 and the Drive phrasing file now list 7/10 for the Full Report (clash already with Rafi), level not changed.
